system: Lund-Mackay CT staging of chronic rhinosinusitis: each of five sinus groups per side graded 0 to 2 and the ostiomeatal complex 0 or 2, totalling 0 to 12 per side and 0 to 24 overall

summary.text: A simple CT staging system for chronic rhinosinusitis: five sinus groups on each side are graded 0 (no abnormality), 1 (partial opacification) or 2 (total opacification).

locator.section: Outline of staging system, paragraph 2 (journal p183)

summary.text: The ostiomeatal complex is scored 0 (not obstructed) or 2 (obstructed). The total is 0 to 24, and each side can be taken separately (0 to 12).

locator.section: Outline of staging system, paragraph 2 (journal p183)

summary.text: Anatomic variants are recorded as present or absent but do not contribute to the score. The paper gives no severity bands and no management for any score.

locator.section: Outline of staging system, paragraph 2 (journal p183) and Table 1 (p184)

summary.text: The authors kept the system deliberately simple. All degrees of partial opacification share one grade, and simplicity may over-state disease extent where secretion rather than mucosal disease causes opacification.

definitions.text: Sinus group grade, scored for each of maxillary, anterior ethmoid, posterior ethmoid, sphenoid and frontal: 0 no abnormality; 1 partial opacification; 2 total opacification.

locator.section: Outline of staging system, paragraph 2 (journal p183)

definitions.text: Ostiomeatal complex (OMC): 0 if not obstructed, 2 if obstructed. No intermediate score of 1.

locator.section: Outline of staging system, paragraph 2 (journal p183)

definitions.text: Total score: sum of the sinus group grades and the OMC score, 0 to 24 overall or 0 to 12 for each side taken separately.

definitions.text: Anatomic variants noted present (1) or absent (0) and not added to the score: absent frontal sinus, concha bullosa, paradoxical middle turbinate, Haller cells, everted uncinate process, agger nasi pneumatization.

pitfalls.text: The paper defines no severity bands, thresholds or management for any total. Library note: a report should state the score (and sides) rather than label it mild, moderate or severe on this paper's authority.

locator.section: Outline of staging system and Table 1 (journal pp183-184)

pitfalls.text: Partial opacification is a single grade (1), whatever its extent, particularly in the maxillary sinus. The authors accept this loss of detail for ease of use and say it may be revised.
The system can over-state disease extent where secretion rather than mucosal disease produces the opacification.

The OMC takes only 0 or 2, never 1. The prose says only 'each sinus group'; the list of five groups (anterior and posterior ethmoids separate) comes from Table 1, so each side has five groups plus the OMC.

locator.section: Table 1: Radiological grading, and Outline paragraph 2 (journal pp183-184)

pitfalls.text: The text states endoscopic appearances are not in the staging system. Variants are stated not to score. The surgical score (own 0 to 14 total) and patient symptom score are separate sections of the form, so we read them as outside the radiological score (inference).

Developed to stage non-neoplastic sinus disease, chiefly chronic rhinosinusitis in patients undergoing endoscopic sinus surgery. The paper was not developed for tumours; it speaks of staging non-neoplastic sinus disease.

The only agreement figure is a 98% correlation of scores between two people (one an author) scoring 200 scans independently; there is no validation against symptoms or outcome. The authors describe the system as a starting point open to modification.

The paper is silent on: how to score an absent or hypoplastic sinus (absent frontal sinus is listed only as a variant); what separates partial from total opacification; what counts as ostiomeatal complex obstruction; and whether post-operative anatomy is scored. The card adds no convention.
